transcriptText:
Your draw missed. Jack-nine, on queen, ten, five, four, two... jack high. 150 in the pot, and he checks. Is that a reason to bluff? Bet 100, or check?

Rewind the hand. You raised, bet the flop, bet the turn... and he called twice. That story says queens or better. His range: 102 combos, an illustration. Rule of thumb: he calls with top pair or better. The other 77 fold... and 74 of them beat you.

Break-even is 40%. He folds 75.5%. That's about 88.7 a bluff. Checking: 4.4. Bet. This time, he calls with queen-jack. One sample... one of the 25 calls the math counted. The verdict stays bet.

Same river... a station who calls with any pair. 18 fold... 17.6%. The bluff loses 55.9 a try. Check. So bluff when the story holds and the hands that fold beat you. A call is one sample, not the grade. Up next: defending against bets.
